Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the MediCore Health Systems Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss MediCore Health Systems' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Marcus Lee, Chief Medical Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Operating Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Strategy Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Information Officer; Karen Mills, Chief Human Resources Officer; and David Ruiz, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on eight key areas: the impact of our recent acquisitions, our strategic priorities and outlook, revenue per admission trends, the effects of seasonality and external factors, labor costs as a percentage of revenue, operating margin performance year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, the results from our cost reduction efforts, and our capital expenditures for facility upgrades and growth.

Let me start with our strategic priorities and outlook. As we close out a strong quarter with revenue growth of 6.2% year-over-year to roughly $2.8 billion, powered by 4.8% higher adjusted admissions and solid outpatient activity, we're honing in on the shifting healthcare environment while seizing opportunities from recovering elective surgeries, an aging population, and the move to value-based models. Across our network of about 180 acute care hospitals and 450 outpatient sites in 28 states, our immediate focus for Q4 is building operational strength against labor tightness and payer pressures. Nursing shortages persist at around 15% vacancy rates per American Hospital Association figures, but our Talent Pipeline Initiative—partnering with 15 nursing schools for fast-track training and committing $50 million to retention incentives and skills platforms—has cut RN agency costs by 22% sequentially. This supports projected core days growth of 3.5% year-over-year, inpatient occupancy at 68% up from 65%, and outpatient visits jumping 12% in orthopedics and cardiology.

We're also sharpening supply chain efforts after last year's hiccups, with a peer consortium including players like HCA and Tenet delivering 9% lower drug costs, especially on generics facing shortages like GLP-1 analogs. Q4 EBITDA margins should widen 50 basis points to 18.2%, aided by $150 million in savings from divesting three low-margin rural sites in the Midwest hit hard by high Medicare Advantage penetration. The Southeast, 35% of our revenue, leads with 7% admission gains in Florida and Texas from migration and Medicaid adjustments, while Northeast urban areas face 2-3% reimbursement squeezes—but our 95% Epic EHR rollout is powering denials recovery of $80 million this quarter.

For full-year 2025, we see revenue up 7-8% to $11.5-$11.8 billion, adjusted admissions rising 5%, outpatient mix to 62% from 58%, and EBITDA at $2.1-$2.2 billion or 18.5-19% margins, assuming stable Medicare IPPS at +2.5%, commercial at 180% of Medicare, and no big CMS shifts on site-neutral rules. This rests on three pillars: digital transformation with $450 million in capex, rolling out AI tools like Nuance DAX in 70% of EDs for 25% less documentation time and $100 million in physician gains, plus Oracle Cerner upgrades and ACO REACH to 2.5 million lives for $250 million in savings; network growth via $1.2 billion in M&A and capex for five new ASCs in Sun Belt spots and tuck-ins in behavioral health and rural emergency hospitals; and patient innovations like our app with Teladoc for telehealth and care plans, lifting Net Promoter Scores to 78, alongside new payer deals with UnitedHealth and Elevance at +4% rates covering 40% commercial.

Risks like 4-5% wage hikes, cyber issues, or FY2026 Medicare trims are offset by boomer-driven ortho demand, GLP-1 bariatric surges, and telehealth extensions. We're set for mid-teens total shareholder returns with 4-6% dividend hikes and $1 billion buybacks.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Sarah to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you, Elena. Good morning, everyone. As Elena highlighted, we had an exceptionally strong quarter. Net revenue for Q3 2024 was $2.05 billion, an increase of 12% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by higher patient volumes, better payer mixes, revenue cycle improvements, and our strategic buys.

Our operating expenses were $1.70 billion, representing 83% of net revenue. We're keeping tight control on costs while funding growth, especially in supply chain areas. Net income for the quarter was $185 million, or $1.45 per diluted share. We're raising our full-year guidance accordingly.

Let me expand on those key financial areas Elena mentioned, starting with the impact of our recent acquisitions—one of the biggest drivers this quarter. We've pursued tuck-in deals to strengthen high-growth regions and high-margin outpatient services, fitting the industry's outpatient and value-based shift. In Q1, we closed the $450 million purchase of Southeast Regional Hospitals, a five-hospital group with 850 beds in Georgia and South Carolina. In Q2, we added Precision Ambulatory Partners for $320 million, running 22 ASCs and three office labs in Florida and Texas. These are paying off quickly.

They added $285 million in net revenue in Q3, 14% of our total, with SRH contributing $210 million—its inpatient revenue up 8% sequentially on a case mix index of 1.85 from 1.72, thanks to ortho and neuro demand from aging boomers. PAP brought $75 million, procedures up 22% quarter-over-quarter from post-COVID backlog and cross-referrals. This lifted same-facility growth by 3 points, countering softer Medicare rates under IPPS FY2024 that cut blended ASP by 50 basis points.

On margins, they generated $68 million EBITDA at 24%, beating our 18% average and adding $0.12 to adjusted EPS. SRH saw $12 million procurement synergies via Vizient GPO, dropping supply costs 7% on implants and stents. PAP's 32% margins leverage fixed costs; case revenue per procedure rose to $4,200 from $3,900 with 45% commercial mix and 98% clean claims from our RCM tools. Integration is smooth: 90% Epic harmonization at SRH cut duplicate charting 40%, aiding population health analytics for $15 million risk-adjustment in Medicare Advantage. Centralized coding and billing saved $8 million SG&A run-rate, with $25 million capex on OR upgrades and two new ASCs in Orlando and DFW.

These position us in Sunbelt growth—4-5% population gains, tightening bed supply, SRH occupancy at 72% from 65% with 15% commercial admission rise. PAP volumes 25% above pre-deal on 340B and site-neutral trends. They speed our hub-and-spoke model, hospitals feeding ASCs as inpatient dips to 60-65% pre-pandemic while outpatient grows 7-9% CAGR on CMS bundles. Like HCA's 200 bps margin gain, we're targeting 250 bps, $45 million full-year synergies 20% ahead of plan. ROIC at 14% over 12% hurdle, 30%+ EPS accretive in 2025. Next, $1.2 billion for bolt-ons in Midwest SNFs and California behavioral health at 22% margins, hedged on staffing with 85% retention.

These build our moat in consolidation.

Next, revenue per admission trends. RPA hit $13,450 in Q3, up 6.2% YoY from $12,660 and 2.1% sequentially from $13,170. Same-facility up 5.8% YoY, TTM at $13,120 from $12,400. It dipped to $12,100 in Q2 2022 on COVID but rebounded; full-year pacing $13,500, topping HCA's 4.5%.

Drivers: payer mix with 48% commercial up from 45%, Medicare 38% steady but MA at 22% adding $450 via HCC; commercial RPA $18,200 up 7.1%, Medicare $12,900 up 4.8% on IPPS 2.9% bump. CMI 1.82 up 3.5% on ortho (DRG 470, CMI 2.15) and cardiology up 12-22%, trimming low-acuity psych. Ancillaries 52% of RPA up from 49%: imaging $2,100 up 11% on GE/Philips scanners, pharmacy $1,850 up 9% via 340B $250 million savings, cath labs $900 on EP cases +18%.

Southeast RPA $14,200 up 8.4% on commercial/ortho; Midwest $12,600 up 3.2%; West $13,800 up 2.9%; Northeast $14,500 up 7.2%. Revenue cycle AI from Change cut denials to 8.2%, A/R to 45 days; Epic/MyChart lifted CMI 0.04; 3M HCC pilots. $150 million ASC JVs shift low-acuity. Outlook 5-7% growth on IPPS 2.8%, VBP top decile.

Moving to seasonality and external factors, like respiratory season. Q3 saw ADC up 18% YoY to 4,250 beds on 22% ED visits (1.2 million) and 14% admissions, respiratory 28% vs. 19%. Revenue up 16% to $2.8 billion, CMI 1.85 flat, commercial 42%. Margins squeezed to 14.2% from 16.1% on $45 million antiviral supplies +25%, agency labor +32%, but full-year added 3 points to 12.8% EBITDA after $120 million costs.

Northeast up 28% ED/24% ADC on weather/RSV; Sunbelt 12% milder. JN.1 COVID added 9% admissions, $85 million outlier pay. SurgeReady AI with Epic cut OT 17%, LOS 0.4 days to 4.2. $250 million capex for 500 ICU beds, Roche testing. Optum VBC 25% Medicare for $40 million savings. Milder 2025 flu expected, $150 million reserves. Tailwind for volumes, headwind margins at 4-5% volatility.

On labor costs as percentage of revenue, at 54.8% up 170 bps YoY from 53.1% but flat QoQ; same-facility 54.5%. Wage inflation: RN 6.2% to match Advisory Board 5.8%, travel 4% hours at 2.1x core down from 2.5x. ED physician locums +4% on CMI 1.42. Sunbelt 56.2% on staffing mandates; Midwest 52.1% low union. Epic/Cerner AI cut OT 12%; Flex Workforce upskilled 2,400 to RN roles, agency -28%; tele-nursing 15% admissions, 300 FTE equivalent saved. Q3 to 54.0-54.5%, FY 54.2-54.7% vs. industry 580 bps 2022 hit. Productivity via OR to 78%, robotics; target low-52% by 2026 like HCA 51.8%.

Operating margins at 9.8%, +160 bps YoY from 8.2%, +70 bps QoQ from 9.1%—sixth straight quarter, matching HCA top end. Revenue +7.2% to $2.85B on 5.8% admissions, 12% surgical, CMI 1.68 +2.1%. Labor +4.1% < revenue via Flex model, RN bonuses $15k, contract -18%; supplies +5.2% vs. 6% inflation, Vizient 8% better pricing. Other OpEx +3.8%, Epic 85% live A/R 42 days, collections 110%. Sunbelt 12.4% +230 bps; Midwest/Northeast 7.2% +110 bps. QoQ on acuity, AI staffing -22% OT, $12M bad debt reversal post-Change cyber. Outpatient 48% +6 points, ASCs 22% margins +18% volumes. Q3 guide 9.5-10.0%, $150M robotics/tele-ICU.

Cost reduction via Bridge to Efficiency: Q3 $112M savings, YTD $285M or 4.2% OpEx cut, +280 bps EBITDA to 18.7%. Labor 42% savings $120M: Oracle AI 85% facilities OT -22% agency -35% $45M; RN ladder turnover 19% to 11.5% PHAPD +8%; Phoenix RCM hub A/R 42 days $28M. Northeast 3.8%, Southeast +18%. Supplies 28% $80M: Vizient 16% pricing, Stryker/Medtronic variance -65% case -11%; Cardinal VMI carrying -24%; biosimilars $22M. Admin/IT 18% $51M: Epic Cogito denials $18M claims 97.5%; Teladoc LOS -0.4 $15M save; divest LTACHs $45M. Facilities $34M. Reinvest 40% $114M ASCs/bundles. FY25 $115M more, cost/case -5.3%.

Finally, capex $285M Q3 8% revenue +18% YoY, YTD $825M to $1.1-1.2B FY. Modernization 62% $177M: $450M Epic Q3 $45M AI RCM denials -15%; $32M Siemens/GE imaging wait -25%; Midwest $50M seismic/OR bariatric; Northeast $28M Mako LOS -10-15%. Expansion 38% $108M: Texas micro-hospitals 150 beds $65M 75% ramp 25% margins; Florida freestanding EDs $25M; California behavioral +40 beds $18M. Payback 3.5 years IRR 18%, 60% revolver. Q4 $260-280M, 2025 $1.25-1.35B ASCs. Supports 4-6% growth, 200 bps margins.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Lee for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Marcus Lee:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning. We are making significant strides in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our integrated care coordination program has delivered a 22% reduction in readmission rates. We're leveraging technology like our telehealth platform, remote patient monitoring, and AI diagnostic tools to enhance experiences and coordination.

Following that, Tom will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Dr. Lee. We are focused on streamlining operations across our network. We've rolled out lean process redesign and AI-driven scheduling, yielding cost savings, better patient throughput, and higher staff output with OR utilization up to 78%.

Next, Lisa will discuss our strategic initiatives.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Tom. Our priorities center on network expansion, new partnerships, and tech investments. We're pursuing growth in key markets, enhancing services, and diversifying revenues through ASCs and behavioral health.

After that, Raj will cover our IT infrastructure and cybersecurity.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. We're dedicated to a secure IT backbone supporting operations and patient data. New measures strengthen cybersecurity, ensure HIPAA and regulatory compliance, and cut breach risks. Cloud migrations boost scalability.

Following that, Karen will discuss workforce development and engagement.

Karen Mills:
Thank you, Raj. We're focused on attracting and retaining top talent. Initiatives include enhanced training, development paths, and diversity efforts to foster inclusion and satisfaction.

Finally, David will elaborate on compliance.

David Ruiz:
Thank you, Karen. We uphold top ethical and regulatory standards. Our program covers all laws, safeguards privacy under HIPAA, and combats fraud through monitoring and training.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, everyone. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions: press star then 1. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
Good morning. Can you provide more details on the specific initiatives you are implementing to improve employee satisfaction and retention?

Karen Mills:
Good morning, Mike. Absolutely. Building on our Talent Pipeline and Flex Workforce efforts Sarah and Elena noted, we've expanded retention bonuses to $15,000 averages for RNs, launched clinical ladders with competency pay, partnered with universities for upskilling 2,400 staff, and integrated AI scheduling to cut overtime 12-22%. Turnover's down to 11.5% from 19%, with tele-nursing easing loads. HCAHPS steady at 4.2 stars, and we're targeting low-52% labor ratio by 2026 through productivity gains.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
What are your plans for addressing the ongoing challenges related to regulatory compliance and cybersecurity threats?

David Ruiz:
Thanks, Emily. Our comprehensive program includes regular audits, Epic-integrated AI for denial and risk prediction, and post-Change Healthcare lessons with enhanced redundancies. We've invested in cloud security, staff training, and real-time monitoring to protect PHI, ensuring 97.5% clean claims and compliance with IPPS, HIPAA, and fraud rules. Contingency planning covers threats like outages.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Can you elaborate on the potential impact of your strategic acquisitions on your long-term growth prospects?

Lisa Chen:
Hi David. The SRH and PAP deals are transformative, adding 14% revenue immediately, 24% EBITDA margins, and positioning our hub-and-spoke model for outpatient shift. Synergies at $45 million ahead of plan, ROIC 14%, 30% EPS boost in 2025. With $1.2 billion more for SNFs and behavioral, we're capturing Sunbelt growth and VBC, targeting 7-8% revenue growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim:
How are you leveraging AI to improve diagnostic accuracy?

Dr. Marcus Lee:
Good morning, Sarah. Our AI tools in Epic Cogito and Nuance DAX cut documentation 25%, boost CMI 0.04 points, and predict readmissions down 14%. In imaging with GE/Philips and cath labs, accuracy rises via spectral tech; HCC pilots add $300/admission. Pilots show 15-20% better outcomes in neuro/cardio, supporting VBC shared savings.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the MediCore Health Systems Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
